# Results — Study 954 (High Yield in Disguise) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The construction: on the
trailing **252 trading days** fit the constrained regression
`r_HY − r_IEF = w · (r_SPY − r_IEF) + residual`, freeze `w` at each **calendar month-end**
and apply it to the **following** month — the study's single execution lag, so the weight
in force on day *t* was fitted on returns ending at least one trading day earlier and is
never re-fitted intra-month. The replication is the fully funded blend
`w · SPY + (1 − w) · IEF`, charged 2 bps one-way on its rebalance turnover (a PROXY, swept
below) and a 50 bps/yr borrow spread on any short leg (a PROXY that is **identically zero**
here — see the weight range). The high-yield fund pays no rebalancing friction at all: it
is bought once and held, so the race is deliberately generous to it. Both arms are then
measured **excess-of-cash** (minus BIL's total return). Daily **total-return** closes
(`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`) — never price-only, which would be a different question
for a fund that pays out 5–8% a year in coupon. As-of **2026-06-30** (the partial current
month is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| HYG (high yield), SPY (equity), IEF (duration), BIL (cash) | 2007-05-30 → 2026-06-30 | 4,802 | Fingerprint `c08a8d88f0f9` |

Held-out record after the first estimation window: **2008-06-02 → 2026-06-30, 4,548 days**.
Cross-checks: JNK and USHY are cached too.

**Survivorship.** The high-yield side is three funds that are *still listed*. Every dead
US high-yield ETF (there have been several small ones) is missing, which biases the fund
side **upward**. The finding below is that the funds still lose — so survivorship makes the
result conservative, not flattering.

## The fitted blend — high yield is roughly 45% equity, 55% duration

| | Value |
|---|--:|
| Mean held-out equity share *w* | **0.450** |
| Range of *w* over 18 years | [0.269, 0.631] |
| Max short notional (would trigger the borrow charge) | **0.000** |
| Replication turnover | 0.34 ×NAV/yr |

The weight never leaves `[0, 1]`, so the replication is a **fully funded long-only blend**
throughout: no leverage, no shorting, and the borrow PROXY is inert by construction. High
yield is not "levered equity" — it is *de-levered* equity plus a large Treasury sleeve.

## Question 1 — is high yield a costume? (no)

| Horizon | n | R² of the replication | Tracking error |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Daily | 4,548 | **0.468** | 8.15%/yr |
| Weekly | 944 | 0.565 | 7.45%/yr |
| Monthly | 217 | 0.517 | 7.18%/yr |
| Quarterly | 73 | 0.591 | 6.26%/yr |

The blend explains barely **half** of high yield's variation, and lengthening the return
horizon barely helps — so this is *not* a stale-marking artefact of an illiquid bond fund.
Roughly 7 pp/yr of tracking error is left over: a genuine, distinct credit-spread risk that
neither SPY nor IEF carries. **The "just levered equity in a bond costume" claim fails on
its own terms.**

The residual of that regression is **−2.16%/yr** with HAC *t* = **−1.25** — negative but on
its own not statistically distinguishable from zero. It is also the *least* robust number
in this document: swap the duration leg for SHY and it shrinks to −0.62%/yr, swap it for
TLT and it triples to −4.19%/yr (see the duration-leg sweep below). Treat it as a
description of *this* blend, not as a measurement of unpaid credit risk.

## Question 2 — does the distinct risk pay? (not on this tape)

Both arms excess-of-cash; drawdowns are the *absolute* (lived) ones. **Two different CAGR
columns, kept apart on purpose:** the *excess* CAGR is what the Sharpe race is run on (the
series after BIL's total return is subtracted), the *lived* CAGR is what the holder's
statement showed. Cash itself compounded at **+1.26%/yr** over this window, which is the
whole of the difference between the two columns.

| Arm | Excess Sharpe | Excess CAGR | **Lived CAGR** | Vol | Max drawdown (lived) | HAC *t* (mean) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **HYG (buy and hold)** | **+0.395** | +3.85% | **+5.17%** | 11.12% | **−32.40%** | +1.73 |
| **Held-out SPY/IEF replication** | **+0.731** | +6.34% | **+7.68%** | 8.96% | **−20.70%** | +3.39 |

- **Excess-Sharpe gap (HYG − replication): −0.336**, vol-matched HAC *t* = **−2.07**. At the
  same realised volatility the replication delivered roughly **3.7 pp/yr** more
  excess-of-cash return than the fund. The vol match uses each arm's **full-sample**
  realised volatility, i.e. it is computed *ex post*: that is the standard Jobson-Korkie
  construction and it is a **test statistic, not a tradable path** — nobody could have
  levered to those constants in advance. Every euro figure quoted in this document (CAGR,
  drawdown, crisis table) comes from the **unscaled** series instead, where the
  replication won by **+2.5 pp/yr** while also running 2.2 pp *less* volatility.
- The replication also took *less* risk on the way (9.0% vol vs 11.1%) and a shallower
  worst loss (−20.7% vs −32.4%).

## Bootstrap CIs (2,000 draws, 21-day blocks)

| Series | Point | 95% CI | share < 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| HYG excess Sharpe | +0.395 | [−0.049, +0.900] | 4.4% |
| Replication excess Sharpe | +0.731 | [+0.314, +1.205] | 0.1% |
| **Vol-matched gap** | **−0.427** | **[−0.805, −0.035]** | 98.4% |

The gap's CI excludes zero — but only just. HYG's own excess-Sharpe CI includes zero.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2017-01-01)

| Era | n | HYG exSharpe | Repl exSharpe | Gap (*t*) | Residual (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2008–2016 | 2,163 | +0.480 | +0.770 | **−0.290** (*t* = −1.19) | −1.07%/yr (*t* = −0.34) |
| 2017–2026 | 2,385 | +0.298 | +0.696 | **−0.398** (*t* = −2.05) | −3.15%/yr (*t* = −1.97) |

Negative in **both** halves, and bigger in the recent one — but only the recent half clears
|*t*| = 2.

## What each side cost in a crisis (absolute, lived)

| Episode | HYG drawdown | Repl drawdown | HYG return | Repl return |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2008 GFC (Jun-08 → Jun-09) | **−32.4%** | −20.7% | −9.2% | −8.9% |
| 2020 Covid (Feb → Apr) | **−22.0%** | −13.1% | −6.9% | **+1.4%** |
| 2022 rate shock (full year) | −15.5% | **−18.9%** | −11.0% | **−15.7%** |

Two out of three go to the replication, and by a wide margin: in both *credit* shocks the
blend's Treasury sleeve rallied while high-yield spreads blew out. The exception is the one
episode that was a **pure duration event** — 2022 — where the replication's larger bond
sleeve is the liability and the fund's shorter-duration, higher-coupon bonds win by 3.4 pp
of drawdown and 4.7 pp of return. The choice is therefore *not* free: swapping the fund for
the blend swaps credit risk for interest-rate risk.

## Cost sensitivity — the friction is a rounding error

The replication rebalances once a month by a few basis points of weight (0.34 ×NAV of
turnover per year), so the cost PROXY barely registers:

| One-way cost | Repl exSharpe | Gap (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +0.732 | −0.337 (*t* = −2.07) |
| 2 bps (headline) | +0.732 | −0.336 (*t* = −2.07) |
| 10 bps | +0.728 | −0.333 (*t* = −2.05) |
| 25 bps (punitive) | +0.723 | −0.328 (*t* = −2.02) |

The gap survives a cost 12× the headline. The borrow PROXY is untested by the data because
the fitted weight never went short.

## Design sensitivity — the estimation window

The one design choice with real bite. A longer fit is a steadier weight but starts the
out-of-sample record later, dropping more of 2008:

| Window | OOS start | n | mean *w* | HYG | Repl | Gap (*t*) | R² |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 126 d | 2007-12-03 | 4,672 | 0.445 | +0.382 | +0.633 | −0.250 (*t* = −1.58) | 0.463 |
| **252 d (headline)** | 2008-06-02 | 4,548 | 0.450 | +0.395 | +0.732 | **−0.336** (*t* = −2.07) | 0.468 |
| 504 d | 2009-06-01 | 4,297 | 0.460 | +0.616 | +0.988 | −0.373 (*t* = −2.32) | 0.560 |
| 756 d | 2010-06-01 | 4,045 | 0.468 | +0.533 | +0.922 | −0.389 (*t* = −2.41) | 0.586 |

The sign is unanimous and the fitted weight is stable at ~0.45 across every window, but the
*t* straddles the bar: −1.58 at the shortest, −2.41 at the longest. The headline uses the
252-day window because it is the shortest one that still gives a steady weight *and* keeps
the entire 2008 crash inside the out-of-sample record — the episode the practical question
is about.

## Design sensitivity — which Treasury is "the" duration leg?

Picking **IEF (7-10y)** is a design choice, not a fact of the tape: a high-yield fund's own
duration is nearer **3-4 years**, so SHY (1-3y) and IEI (3-7y) are at least as defensible
and TLT (20y+) is the aggressive end. The weight re-fits itself to whatever leg it is
given, so the *fit* always works; the question is whether the *conclusion* does. Same
common sample (2008-06-02 → 2026-06-30, 4,548 days), same everything else. **Treasury legs
only** — putting AGG or LQD on the bench would smuggle the credit risk under test into the
benchmark.

| Duration leg | mean *w* | R² | Residual | Repl exSharpe | Gap (*t*) | Repl worst DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SHY (1-3y) | 0.357 | 0.478 | **−0.62%/yr** | +0.692 | −0.297 (*t* = **−1.93**) | −18.96% |
| IEI (3-7y) | 0.393 | 0.480 | −1.33%/yr | +0.718 | −0.323 (*t* = −2.07) | −20.09% |
| **IEF (7-10y, headline)** | 0.450 | 0.468 | −2.16%/yr | +0.732 | **−0.336** (*t* = **−2.07**) | −20.70% |
| TLT (20y+) | 0.614 | 0.415 | **−4.19%/yr** | +0.739 | −0.344 (*t* = **−1.92**) | −27.59% |

Two things fall out of this table, and only one of them flatters the study:

1. **The direction is leg-proof.** Every maturity from 1-3y to 20y+ hands the replication
   the higher excess Sharpe, by a gap of −0.30 to −0.34. Nothing here is a maturity bet.
2. **The *t* is not.** The headline |*t*| = 2.07 is the **top** of a range that runs down to
   **1.93** (SHY) and **1.92** (TLT) — so the bar is cleared at the middle maturities and
   missed at both ends. Read with the estimation-window sweep (|*t*| from 1.58 to 2.41),
   this is a result whose *sign* is unanimous across every design choice we can vary and
   whose *significance* flickers around the bar depending on which defensible choice you
   make. That is the whole case for the **Mixed** stamp rather than Real.

The residual is even more leg-dependent than the gap: **−0.62%/yr against SHY and
−4.19%/yr against TLT**. Most of the headline **−2.16%/yr** is therefore the *price of the
maturity mismatch* (IEF is roughly twice HY's duration and this window was kind to bonds),
not a clean measure of unpaid credit risk. Only the vol-matched race, which cannot be
gamed by handing an arm more duration risk, is comparable across the four legs.

## Cross-checks — the other two high-yield funds

| Fund | Window | n | mean *w* | R² | Gap (*t*) | Residual (*t*) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| JNK | 2009-01 → 2026-06 | 4,399 | 0.443 | 0.487 | −0.268 (*t* = −1.64) | −1.17%/yr (*t* = −0.79) |
| USHY | 2018-11 → 2026-06 | 1,923 | 0.367 | 0.630 | −0.286 (*t* = −1.24) | −2.34%/yr (*t* = −1.18) |

Same sign, same magnitude, same ~0.37–0.45 equity share — but **neither clears |*t*| = 2**
on its own shorter sample.

## Where part of the gap comes from — the fee (a PROXY decomposition)

Quoted net expense ratios: HYG **0.49%**, SPY 0.0945%, IEF 0.15% → a 45/55 blend costs
**0.125%**. That 0.365 pp/yr advantage is already inside both total-return tapes (nothing is
double-counted); it accounts for roughly a **sixth** of the −2.16%/yr residual. The rest is
the credit risk itself failing to pay over this particular eighteen years.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

The generator builds a fund that *is* `0.45 × equity + 0.55 × duration` plus a credit shock
of fixed size; only the shock's *price* changes.

| World | fitted *w* | R² | Residual (*t*) | Gap (*t*) | Gap over 8 seeds |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Uncompensated shock (3%/yr give-up) | 0.456 | 0.653 | −3.79%/yr (*t* = −2.65) | **−0.511** (*t* = −3.56) | mean −0.437, sd 0.129 |
| Fairly paid shock (**the null**) | 0.456 | 0.653 | +0.15%/yr (*t* = +0.11) | −0.126 (*t* = −0.88) | mean **−0.050**, sd 0.128, fires 0/8 |

The harness recovers the planted weight to within 0.006 in *both* worlds, finds the planted
give-up, and stays quiet when the same extra risk is fairly compensated. The real-tape
result is therefore a property of the high-yield tape, not of the harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Mixed.** The study asks two questions and the tape answers them differently.
  The *disguise* half is **refuted**: the equity + duration blend explains only R² = 0.47
  daily (0.52–0.59 at longer horizons) and leaves ~7 pp/yr of tracking error, so high yield
  is a genuinely distinct risk and not a repackaged equity position. The *compensation* half
  points one way everywhere — the replication out-Sharpes the fund by 0.25 to 0.39 across
  every estimation window, both eras and all three funds, never once with the opposite sign
  — but the evidence is **marginal**: the headline HAC *t* is −2.07, the bootstrap CI on the
  gap is [−0.805, −0.035] (barely clear of zero), the 2008–2016 era gives *t* = −1.19, the
  standalone residual gives *t* = −1.25, JNK (−1.64) and USHY (−1.24) both miss the bar,
  and swapping the duration leg for SHY (−1.93) or TLT (−1.92) drops the headline back
  under it. One unanimous direction, one bar that is only just cleared and that two
  perfectly defensible design choices un-clear: that is Mixed, not Real.
- **Tradability — Fragile.** The practical swap is real and cheap to run: 0.34 ×NAV/yr of
  turnover, cost-insensitive out to 25 bps, no leverage or borrow, **+2.5 pp/yr of lived
  CAGR** (7.68% vs 5.17%; the same +2.5 pp excess-of-cash) and −11.7 pp of worst drawdown
  over eighteen years. But it is a **substitution, not an
  alpha** — you keep the risk premia and drop a fund fee — and it fails in the one regime
  it is most likely to be sold into: in the 2022 rate shock the blend lost 4.7 pp *more*
  than the fund, because trading credit risk for duration risk is exactly what it does. A
  holder is buying a different exposure, not a free lunch, and the *t* backing the swap is
  2.07 on a single fund.
- **Named non-tape inputs.** The one-way cost (2 bps), the borrow spread (50 bps/yr,
  inert — the weight never went short), the three crisis calendar windows, the estimation
  window (252 d), **the choice of IEF as the duration leg**, the SPY equity leg, the
  2017-01-01 era split and the quoted expense ratios are all PROXIES or design choices;
  every one of them is swept or shown to be inert above, except the equity leg (SPY is the
  US market, which is what the folklore claim names) and the era split (a round mid-sample
  date). The vol-matched difference is an **ex-post** construction — a test statistic, not
  a portfolio.
- **Survivorship.** Named on the Signal axis: three still-listed funds, dead high-yield
  ETFs absent, which biases the *fund* side up and therefore makes the negative finding
  conservative.
